engagement_title: Emberwell Brew House spring insert: turn fourteen retyped menus into one merge system driven by the operations price sheet, recover the mark off the apron pin, split the four kitchenless counter rooms onto their own card driven by a second template, carry each room's own address, hours and rotating on now line off the operations store directory, and settle what a store that does not serve a dish actually prints
vertical: Food, restaurant and beverage, a fourteen room independent brew house and coffee group across New England, mixed format estate with two flagship kitchens and four counter service rooms
real_brief_anchor: ADAPTED from the real Upwork cafe menu brief carried in this entry's real_brief_anchors: a neighbourhood brew cafe seeking a designer with 'Proficiency in Adobe InDesign' and a 'Strong sense of typography, layout, and print design', to deliver a full food and drinks menu, print ready files, and editable InDesign source, in a style the client described as 'warm, cozy, and elevated'. The real client and persona are laundered to the FICTIONAL Emberwell Brew House, and no real company, person, product or trademark is named. The prior draft's coined name collided with an existing card game trademark and has been replaced. REPOSITIONED for connector reality, and this is why the verdict is REBUILD rather than STRENGTHEN: the raw posting implies a single menu designed from scratch, which is neither a full commission nor connector work, since from scratch free form print layout is not producible. The honest fuller commission this client genuinely has is the one their own operations reality creates. Fourteen rooms, one brand, fourteen managers retyping the same insert in a word processor until the prices drift, an existing printed insert whose press file the printer still holds, and a price and availability sheet the operations manager already maintains. That is a genuine record per page variable data run with a real template supplied as a client asset, it carries the same 'print ready files and editable source' deliverable the real posting asked for, and it absorbs AO-78. Every name, room, town and dish in the build is North American.
client_one_liner: Fourteen managers retyping the same insert in a word processor, and by March a customer asked why a flat white cost a dollar more twenty minutes down the road.
client_brief:
Emberwell Brew House, spring insert

We run fourteen brew houses across New England. Same name, same room, same coffee program, but the estate is not one price. Portsmouth and Burlington are our flagship rooms with a full plates menu. Four of the newer stores are counter service and do not run a kitchen at all. Everywhere pays a different rent, so prices move by store.

Until now each manager has retyped the insert in a word processor. Fourteen stores, fourteen versions, and by March they had drifted so far apart that a customer at one store asked why a flat white cost a dollar more twenty minutes down the road.

We want one system. One design, built once, with every store's insert coming out of the price and availability sheet our operations manager already keeps.

Some dishes are not offered everywhere. Those stores must not show them, and there must not be a hole on the page where they were.

We printed last season's insert and our printer still has the file. Use it. We are not redesigning, we are making it work.

The four counter rooms are a different problem. They have no kitchen, so a plates insert with every plate struck out is not a shorter menu, it is a broken one. They ran their own smaller card last season, drinks and the pastry case only, and the printer holds that file too. Use both files.

Every insert has to carry that room's own street address and its own hours at the foot, and the one line our operations manager keeps for what is on right now at that room, a tap or a special. All of that lives in the store directory she keeps next to the price sheet, and it has to land on the right room. A counter room cannot advertise a plate it has no kitchen to make.

The look is warm, cozy and elevated. We are not a chain and we do not want to read like one. Plates run fourteen to twenty six dollars, drinks four fifty to seven. Our customer is thirty to fifty five, comes in the morning and stays for two hours. Type led, generous, and the prices set quietly so they do not shout across the page.

What we need. One file the printer can take for the whole estate. A single file per store as well, so each manager can check their own before anything goes to press, because they will find things we do not.

Our old logo file is gone. The enamel pin on the apron is the cleanest version left.

One dish photograph per store, and they were not all shot on the same day. Two of the seasonal items we have never photographed at all.

And one counter card for launch week that we can edit ourselves.
price_band_and_audience: Upper middle independent: plates 14 to 26 dollars, drinks 4.50 to 7, guest 30 to 55, morning trade that lingers, in secondary New England towns where this is the good room rather than the cheap one. The band is load bearing on this task specifically because the whole estate runs through one template, so the register is set once and either fits or does not. At this band the insert is type led and generous, the dish photograph is a single silhouetted plate given air rather than a grid of tiles, prices sit small and quiet at the end of a line, and there are no combos, no starbursts and no value language anywhere. The identical data run at a value fast casual band would correctly be price loud, combo driven, photograph dense and tightly packed, and shipping that here turns a fourteen dollar plate into a food court item and tells the guest they are in the wrong kind of room. Push the other way into tasting menu austerity, no photograph at all and prices hidden on request, and a room whose trade is morning coffee reads as unapproachable and intimidating. An agent that finds a look before it reads the price sheet will land on one of the two extremes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,100 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An independent fourteen room brew house and coffee group across New England, with two flagship kitchens and four counter service coffee rooms.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2013, first room in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. Fourteen rooms across New England, two flagship kitchens, four counter service rooms, one shared coffee program.
brand_identity.about: Emberwell runs fourteen rooms under one name and one coffee program, each in a secondary New England town where it is the good room rather than the cheap one. Same room, same welcome, but every store pays its own rent, so the estate is one brand at fourteen prices.
brand_identity.audience: Morning trade aged 30 to 55 that comes in early and lingers for two hours. Guests who read a menu the way they read a good book and treat loud pricing as a sign they are in the wrong kind of room.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Upper middle independent. Plates 14 to 26 dollars, drinks 4.50 to 7. Not a chain and never wanting to read like one: type led, generous, prices set quietly at the end of a line. No combos, no starbursts, no value language.
brand_identity.typography: A warm high contrast serif for dish names and headings, generously leaded, paired with a quiet humanist sans for descriptions and prices. Between the rustic chalkboard cliche and the cold Swiss default: elevated, never shouting.
brand_identity.voice: Warm and plainspoken, a room talking rather than a brand selling. Short lines, no adjectives stacked for effect. Example: The stout is on until the barrel is done, then it is not.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our old logo file is gone. The cleanest surviving version of the mark is the enamel pin on the apron, of which we hold a close photograph. Approved dish names, descriptions, the drinks list, seasonal line names and the fixed allergen statement all survive as plain text, alongside the public store roster.
brand_identity.values: One consistent welcome across the estate, and honest local pricing that a guest never has to question from one town to the next.

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_price_availability.csv (14 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The operations manager's working sheet, one row per store, carrying the store name and town, every menu line's price for that store, and whether that store offers each line.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the sheet we already keep. It is the only place the real prices live."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A dish a store does not offer arrives as an empty price cell rather than as an absent line, and the merge has no conditional logic and cannot suppress a line, so an untreated empty cell prints a naked dish name with its leader rule running to nothing. Two store names carry a trailing space and one town is spelled two different ways across the sheet, so per store filenames diverge from the roster unless the data is cleaned before anything is bound.

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_insert_spring_prior.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for last season's insert, one page, carrying the dish list, the drinks column, one placed dish photograph and the mark as printed artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last season's, straight from the printer. We are not redesigning it, we are making it work."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its dish names and their prices were set as one continuous flow, so the converted document does not expose a separate price frame no matter how the printed column reads, and every price has to be reached by position inside a shared story. The file also carries no bleed and none can be introduced through conversion, so any press expectation of a bleeding edge cannot be met from this source and has to be stated rather than assumed. It also carries, below the allergen line, a small fixed height footer set to one sample store's address and hours, and a one line frame above the plates for the room's rotating on now line; both were set to that one short sample, so a per store address, hours line or feature of any real length oversets these frames and clips at trim once the merge drives them.

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_counter_card_prior.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for last season's counter card, the smaller drinks and case insert the four kitchenless rooms run: the drinks list, the pastry case line, one rotating on now line, and a footer carrying one sample store's address and hours. No dish photograph and no plates section.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The counter rooms' own card, straight from the printer. The rooms with no kitchen run this, not the plates insert."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a second template with a different structure from the plates file, so a mapping built for one does not transfer: the drink names and their prices are set as one tab aligned two column story rather than the plates file's single flow, the price offsets sit at different positions, and there is no graphic frame anywhere because this tier carries no photograph, so the per store picture column has nothing to bind into on this template and must not be sent to it. Its footer and its on now line were set to one short sample store, so any address, hours or feature of real length oversets and clips at trim on merge, and like the plates file it carries no bleed.

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_store_directory.csv (14 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The operations manager's store directory kept next to the price sheet: one row per store carrying that room's street address, its opening hours and the one line rotating on now feature, all as text. This is where the non numeric per store content on both templates comes from.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Addresses, hours and what is on right now, per room. This is the other sheet I keep."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It has to be joined to the price sheet on the store name to build the merge data, and it carries the clean roster spellings, so the price sheet's two trailing space names miss the join in silence and those rooms merge with an empty footer that no error reports. One counter room's rotating line names a plate its kitchenless room cannot make, so the feature is not a field to pass through but a value to reconcile against the service model. The hours are written a different way on almost every row, and one room's address and one room's on now line are long enough to overset the fixed footer and feature frames both templates inherited from their single sample press files.

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_dish_photos/ (6 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Dish and pour photographs shot in the Portsmouth room across two mornings, all on the same dark walnut counter, natural window light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our own pictures. Two mornings, same counter, same window."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The stout pour and the cortado sit at almost the value of the walnut at the glass shoulder, so a one call knockout returns a clean complete looking cutout that has quietly bitten the rim on exactly those frames, and the bite is invisible against a dark ground and obvious against cream. Two of the six are the same seasonal plate shot twice from slightly different angles, which leaves one store's featured line with no photograph of its own.

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_pin.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Close photograph of the enamel apron pin carrying the house mark: a compound lockup of a kettle silhouette inside a ring of letterspaced small caps, struck in two enamel colours on plated metal.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The pin on the apron. It is the cleanest version of the mark we still have anywhere."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup on a curved reflective surface, so a prompt naming the pin returns the pin rather than the mark, a compound prompt returns the type ring while silently dropping the kettle, and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because the enclosed interior cannot be punched. The plating throws a specular band across the lower left of the ring where the enamel and the metal run to the same value.

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: approved dish names and their descriptions, the drinks list, the seasonal line names, and the allergen statement.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The wording as approved. The allergen line cannot change."

assets_supplied.name: emberwell_store_roster.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The fourteen store names and towns as the group writes them publicly, plus which four rooms are counter service with no kitchen.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we actually write the store names. The four counter service rooms are marked."

acceptance_bar: Page count equals the delivered store count and the pages sit in roster order, with every store present exactly once.
Every price on every page is that store's own price from the sheet, and no price from one store appears on another store's page.
A store that does not offer a line does not show that line, and there is no hole, no orphaned leader rule and no naked dish name where it was.

A kitchenless counter room prints from the counter card template, drinks and the case only, rather than a plates page with every plate struck out, and the two tiers combine into one estate PDF with each room in its own roster slot rather than the counter rooms clumped at the end.
Every page carries that room's own street address, hours and rotating on now line joined from the store directory, none blank where a name was not reconciled, and none showing another room's details.

No address, hours or on now line oversets or clips at trim on any page, and the rotating line at a counter room names something that room can actually serve rather than a plate it has no kitchen to make.
No dish name, description or price is cut off at trim on any page.
Every store's insert carries the dish photograph that belongs to it, and no photograph stands in for two different lines.
Cutouts hold at their edges on cream at trim, on the dark pours as well as on the light plates. A rim that is clean against a dark ground and bitten against cream fails.
The licensed frames sit inside the house set rather than beside it. A bought picture that reads as bought fails even if it is beautiful.
No delivered image exceeds the pixel dimensions it arrived at, and nothing reaches its required size by being enlarged.

Per store files are named to the roster exactly as the group writes its store names, and each file contains that store and no other. A manager who opens a file with their name on it and finds another store's prices is the failure that kills the system.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath it, the kettle and the ring both intact, and still reading at the size it actually prints on the insert.

The insert reads as a fourteen to twenty six dollar independent room: type led, generous, prices quiet. Combo language, price emphasis or a dense photograph grid fails on register even if every field is correct.

The counter card arrives as a working file the group can edit itself plus the self contained source it was built from, and the print expectations that cannot be met from the supplied press file are stated rather than left implied.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, template construction and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, outputSpecs, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (resolution, pageRange, createSeparateFiles)
adobe_surfaces.role: The system the client is actually buying. Two of last season's press files are reverse engineered into two live merge templates, a plates template for the ten kitchen rooms and a drinks only counter card for the four kitchenless rooms, each with its own exposed frame granularity that is not under the agent's control. Every room's prices, its own dish photograph on the kitchen tier, and its address, hours and rotating on now line joined from the store directory are bound per record; the two tiers are merged separately and combined into one estate press PDF with every room in its roster slot; and the estate is also delivered as per store single page files named to the roster through the route whose record identity is guaranteed rather than the route whose labels lie.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Brings six frames shot across two mornings and two licensed frames to one house look, knocks the featured pours and plates out for the silhouetted placement the register calls for, and recovers the mark at ink level off a curved reflective enamel pin with the polarity, compound lockup and vector hygiene decisions the tracing tool does not make. It also derives the transparent raster of the mark that a merge template can actually carry.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the two seasonal items the group has never photographed, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded, then has to make them belong to a set shot on one walnut counter in one window's light. The Boards half persists the shortlist the fourteen managers sign off from before anything goes to press, placed within the per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The launch week counter card the group asked to edit itself, authored as one document carrying two roots at two canvas sizes, an A5 counter card and a square post. It is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Photographs must be embedded as image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the recovered mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the counter card and the written record of what the insert is set in. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so warm, cozy and elevated is the agent's own art direction and has to avoid both the rustic chalkboard cliche and the cold Swiss default. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface and which of the two supplied press files drives which tier of rooms before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The estate run is a variable data job because one store equals one page at volume, and it is a two template job because the four kitchenless rooms cannot run the plates layout at all. The counter card the group edits itself is a one off composition and belongs on the authoring surface, and it cannot be promised as a print file. The brief pins both destinations and both tiers, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and template per tier, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role, including both press files and the store directory.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because fourteen stores, six frames, two press files and two data sheets become indistinguishable URLs quickly.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the price and availability sheet against the roster: clean the store names to the form the group actually writes, reconcile the two spellings, and decide what a store that does not offer a line will print.
trajectory.judgement: The merge prints exactly what the data says and has no conditional logic, so a line cannot be suppressed by the layout. The only place the availability rule can live is in the value written into the field, which makes this a data decision disguised as a design one. The four counter service rooms with no kitchen make the question unavoidable rather than marginal.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned merge dataset with the availability rule applied in the data and written down, plus a delivered store set reconciled to the roster.

trajectory.action: Join the store directory to the cleaned price sheet on the store name to bring each room's address, hours and rotating on now line onto its row, assign every room to a tier so the four kitchenless rooms go to the counter card and the ten kitchen rooms to the plates insert, and reconcile each on now line against that room's service model.
trajectory.judgement: The merge takes one data source per template, so the two sheets have to become two joined datasets, one per tier, before anything is bound. The join is on the store name, which is exactly the field the raw sheet spells with trailing spaces, so an unclean name drops the whole footer in silence rather than raising an error. The on now line is content the merge passes through untouched, so a counter room advertising a plate it has no kitchen for is a value to fix in the data, not a layout the design can catch.
trajectory.produces: Two joined merge datasets, one per tier, with address, hours and a tier appropriate feature on every row and every join miss resolved.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the pin: an ink level selection worded by the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's returned bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed. Derive a transparent raster of the same mark at the scale the insert needs.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the enamel and not the plating, which polarity to trace, and whether the compound lockup came back whole or quietly missing its kettle. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring and returns a plausible solid disc.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent vector mark plus the raster of it a merge template can carry.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's plates press file to a native document, export its structure, and inventory what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, what each story really contains, where each price sits inside it, and how the footer and the on now frames were sized.
trajectory.judgement: The printed column is not evidence of the document's structure. Conversion granularity is a property of how the PDF was produced and is not controllable, so a mapping cannot be designed before the inventory is read, and the footer and feature frames were set to one short sample so their real height is not what the printed page suggests.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory of the plates template with real bounds, applied type, graphic frames and the true story text of every text frame including the footer and feature frames.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping for the plates template against that inventory, run it through the validator, prepare the merge template, then read the prepared document back and check its stories for every placeholder the mapping was supposed to write: prices, dish fields, the joined footer address and hours, and the on now line.
trajectory.judgement: A successful response is not evidence that a mapping landed, and on a document whose prices share one story with the dish names, every price offset depends on the exact string the story really holds rather than on what the printed page looks like.
trajectory.produces: A prepared plates merge template plus a read back record of which placeholders are genuinely present.

trajectory.action: Convert the counter card press file to its own native document, export its structure, and inventory what THIS file exposes, which is not what the plates file did: a tab aligned two column drinks story with the prices at different offsets, no graphic frame at all, and its own footer and on now frames. Build and validate its mapping, prepare it, and read it back.
trajectory.judgement: A second template is a second reverse engineering from scratch: the price offsets, the story count and the absence of any picture frame are all properties of how this file was set, and a mapping copied from the plates template binds to nothing here. There is no graphic frame, so the picture column must not be sent to this tier.
trajectory.produces: A prepared counter card merge template with its placeholders confirmed by read back and its lack of a picture frame recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview and triage the six dish frames for the kitchen tier: which line each actually shows, which two are the same plate, which sit off level, and which stores are left without a photograph of their own. Straighten what needs it.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts one photograph per store. The pictures are the only thing that can settle whether that is six different lines, and straightening reframes the subject so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering line identity, level and duplication, plus a named list of the lines with no photograph.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the two seasonal items nobody photographed, filter to photography, exclude generative tech candidates, license and download at full resolution, and put the downloaded frames beside the house frames.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to a walnut counter in window light rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: Two licensed camera scale frames, downloaded and placed beside the house set.

trajectory.action: Bring every frame, house and licensed, to one house target with a call per frame, using masked corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong.
trajectory.judgement: One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot on two different mornings plus two bought elsewhere. The target is a set, and the licensed frames have to reach it by a different route than the house ones.
trajectory.produces: A graded dish set with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Knock the featured items out to transparency for the silhouetted placement the register calls for, reading every returned tradeoff report rather than the success message, and crop each to the insert's photo frame without enlarging.
trajectory.judgement: Silhouetting on cream is what makes a fourteen dollar plate read as the good room rather than a food court tile, and it is also the treatment that punishes any cutout whose edge does not hold. The tradeoffs object is the only channel that reports what a tool did to the frame's dimensions.
trajectory.produces: Transparent dish cutouts cropped to the frame, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Bind the per store dish photograph column and the mark into the prepared plates template, merge the ten kitchen rooms to their run, and check the page count against the kitchen tier store set.
trajectory.judgement: The image column needs its prefixed header, bare filenames in the cells and file keys matching those filenames exactly. A naive binding places one static photograph on every store and looks completely correct until two towns share a plate that only one of them serves.
trajectory.produces: A merged kitchen tier run, one store per page.

trajectory.action: Merge the four counter rooms from the counter card template with no picture column bound, then combine the kitchen run and the counter run into one estate press PDF with every room sitting in its own roster slot rather than the counter rooms appended at the end.
trajectory.judgement: Each merge preserves only its own subset's order, so concatenating the two runs kitchen then counter passes page count and every store present once yet puts the four counter rooms out of sequence. The counter rooms sit at roster positions nine to twelve, in the middle, so the combined run has to be interleaved to the roster, not stacked by tier.
trajectory.produces: One estate press PDF assembled from both tiers in true roster order.

trajectory.action: Render the merged estate run at print resolution and read every page at trim: every price against the sheet, every unavailable line, every cutout edge on cream, the mark at the size it prints, and the joined footer and on now line on every page for the right room, blank and overset alike.
trajectory.judgement: Nothing before this point shows the page as the printer will print it or as the guest will hold it. Page count agreeing with store count says the run assembled, not that any given page is right, and a footer that is blank or clipped raises no error on merge.
trajectory.produces: Print resolution proofs of the estate run, read at trim.

trajectory.action: Produce the per store single page files across both tiers through the route whose record identity is guaranteed, naming each to the roster exactly as the group writes its store names.
trajectory.judgement: There is more than one route to per record files and they do not all preserve identity. Choosing the trustworthy one is the whole decision, because a manager opening a file with their store's name on it and finding another store's prices is what ends the system.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen named single page insert files, one per delivered store.

trajectory.action: Produce the manager proofs the group asked for and read each one against the price sheet, store by store, before any of them leaves the studio.
trajectory.judgement: The managers were promised a file each to check. A proof set that is internally mislabelled is worse than no proof set, because it sends fourteen people looking for errors in the wrong document.
trajectory.produces: A verified proof set, each proof reconciled to its store's row.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: Warm, cozy and elevated is the agent's own pairing, judged against a fourteen to twenty six dollar room in a secondary New England town. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a heavy weight.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying two roots at two canvas sizes, embed every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload the file, run the readiness check and export, then verify through the two channels that exist.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The rendition shows the first artboard only, so the second canvas can be checked no other way than by reading the returned markup.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document plus the self contained source HTML, with both canvases audited.

trajectory.action: Persist the selects board the managers sign off from, adding the graded set within the per call cap and re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the price and availability formatting note, the field mapping verification note, and the store directory rules covering the join key, the tier split and the feature reconciliation.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success and the vector mark is not boardable, so it belongs in the note instead. The notes have to state the availability rule, the naming rule, the tier rule, how the directory joins, and what the two supplied press files cannot deliver, or next season the estate drifts again.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, plus the written notes and the assembled delivery.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the licensed frames actually look like. Selection happens against a small catalogue thumbnail, and the frame's real colour, its real white balance and everything living at the edges of it exist only once the full resolution file has been licensed and pulled down. Two frames that were indistinguishable at thumbnail scale can sit a long way apart from a set shot on one walnut counter in one window's light, and one of them can carry a cast, a competing surface or a second dish at its edge that the thumbnail simply did not resolve. Whether the chosen frame can be brought to the house target at all, rather than merely adjusted toward it, is only answerable with the downloaded file placed beside the graded house frames.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because there is no higher resolution view before licensing and no metadata field that reports colour or content at the edges. Licensing first and looking after IS the correct order, which is exactly what makes the finding arrive after a commitment. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that two seasonal items were never photographed. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is either a different licensed frame chosen on different grounds, or a masked correction route the house frames never needed, and both change what the graded set contains.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Put the downloaded frames beside the graded house set, judge them there rather than in isolation, and either license an alternative and grade it from scratch or build a confined correction for the bought frame alone, then re judge the whole set as a set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of fourteen stores printing a featured dish that visibly comes from somebody else's kitchen, on an insert whose entire claim is that this is an independent room and not a chain.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the two template estate run actually assembles into once both tiers are merged and combined. Three things surface only here. The counter rooms come back correctly ordered within their own four page run and the kitchen rooms within theirs, so a combine that stacks the tiers passes page count and uniqueness while sitting the four counter rooms at the back instead of at roster positions nine to twelve. The directory join, done on a store name the raw sheet spells with trailing spaces, silently produced empty address and hours for the unreconciled rooms, and an empty joined field merges as a blank footer with no error, exactly as an unavailable price merges as a blank line. And the footer and on now frames, inherited at the size of one short sample store, overset on the rooms whose address or feature runs long, pushing the tail out of the frame where the merge reports success and only the document's overset state or the trim render shows it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because each merge can only order its own subset, an empty joined value is indistinguishable from any other empty field to the merge, and overset is a property of a fixed frame meeting a variable length string that exists only once real records flow through it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for one file for the estate and for each room's own address and hours, not for how a two template run concatenates or how long a given room's address is. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a re interleave of the combined run to roster order, a re clean of the join keys so the missing footers fill, and a frame that auto sizes or a value shortened in the data, all different operations from running the same merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re interleave the two tier runs to true roster order, clean the join keys and re join so no room merges with a blank footer, auto size or enlarge the footer and feature frames or shorten the offending values in the data, then re merge, re combine and re read the affected pages at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An estate PDF in which the four counter rooms sit out of sequence at the back, two kitchen rooms print with no address or hours at the foot, and the flagship room's on now line is clipped mid sentence at trim, shipped as the one file the whole system was bought to produce.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cutout edges hold where they are actually placed. The pours were shot on dark walnut and the stout and the cortado sit at almost the value of the counter at the glass shoulder, so the one call knockout has no contrast to work from at exactly that boundary. It returns a clean, complete, correct looking cutout and reports full success, and against a dark ground the result is genuinely indistinguishable from a good one. The bite only becomes visible when the silhouette lands on cream at trim, which is the register's whole reason for silhouetting in the first place. Which frames are affected is a property of each photograph's own local contrast and cannot be read off the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the knockout has to happen before placement and the evidence only exists after placement. Doing it right the first time would require knowing which of six frames shares luminance with the counter at the subject boundary, which nothing reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the photographs were not all shot on the same day, which is about grading, not edges, and the acceptance line about edges holding on cream is the client's standing quality requirement rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the affected frames go through a different chain, a material named selection of the counter surface inverted and filled, rather than the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the affected frames through an explicit selection worded to the counter's own material properties, inverted and filled, inspect each new edge against cream rather than against the original ground, re bind them, re merge and read the affected pages at trim again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Featured plates on the flagship pages sitting on cream with a chewed rim along one shoulder, at press, across an estate wide print run.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the proof set the managers are about to receive actually says what its labels say. The proofs are requested per store, and the obvious route produces one file per row with the response labelling them in row order, at full success and with no warning of any kind. The labels can be wrong, and the resolution requested for the proof can be silently disregarded so that what comes back is a screen scale image rather than the press scale one that was asked for. Neither is reported anywhere in the response, and both are only discoverable by opening the returned files and reading the store name and the prices on each against the sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the parameter that should control it is accepted and then ignored, and the ordering that should be guaranteed is asserted by the response itself. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that each manager needs their own file to check. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different production route entirely, merging to a native document and rendering separate files from it, or looping the merge one record at a time so identity is guaranteed by construction.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the labelled multi record route, re produce every per store file through a route whose record identity is guaranteed by construction, rename each from its own content rather than from its position in a response, and read a sample of them back against the price sheet before any of them leaves.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen managers each checking a file with their own store's name on it and another store's prices inside, signing off on a run that then prints wrong in every room, which is precisely the drift the commission was bought to end.

deliverables.name: Emberwell estate insert run
deliverables.spec: One press PDF for the whole estate, one delivered store per page in roster order, page count equal to the delivered store count, every price that store's own, every unavailable line resolved with no hole and no orphaned rule, nothing truncated at trim. Delivered alongside the per store single page files named exactly as the group writes its store names, one per store, produced through the route whose record identity is guaranteed. The four kitchenless rooms are merged from the counter card template and the ten kitchen rooms from the plates template, and the two tiers combine into this one PDF with every room in its own roster slot. Every page carries that room's own address, hours and rotating on now line joined from the store directory, on the right room and within trim.

deliverables.name: Live insert merge template
deliverables.spec: One working merge document reverse engineered from the supplied press file, carrying live placeholders for every per store field and a bound image frame for the featured dish, built on the strategy the converted structure actually permits rather than on what the printed column suggests, and read back to prove what it contains. This is the half the group keeps: next season they change the sheet, not the design. Delivered with a plain statement of what the supplied press file cannot provide, including bleed. This is the plates tier template for the ten kitchen rooms, and it also carries live placeholders for the joined footer address, hours and the rotating on now line.

deliverables.name: Live counter card merge template
deliverables.spec: A second working merge document reverse engineered from the supplied counter card press file, structurally its own thing rather than a copy of the plates template: a tab aligned two column drinks story with placeholders for the counter tier's prices, a footer for the joined address and hours, and a frame for the rotating on now line, with no graphic frame because this tier carries no photograph. This is what the four kitchenless rooms run, and it is the half the group keeps for those rooms: next season they change the sheet, not the design. Delivered with a plain statement of what the supplied press file cannot provide, including bleed.

deliverables.name: Recovered Emberwell mark
deliverables.spec: The compound kettle and ring lockup recovered from a photograph of an enamel pin as placeable scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, the kettle and the letterspaced ring both intact, delivered with the transparent raster derived from it for placement, and holding at the size it actually prints on the insert.

deliverables.name: House dish photography set
deliverables.spec: Six house frames and two licensed camera scale frames brought to one house target with a per frame parameter log, straightened where needed, silhouetted to transparency for placement on cream with edges that hold on the dark pours as well as the light plates, cropped to the insert's photo frame with no output exceeding its source pixel dimensions. One picture per featured line with none standing in for two, and any line left without a picture named rather than filled.

deliverables.name: Launch week counter card and handover
deliverables.deliverable_class: editable Express collateral and brand handover document
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying an A5 counter card and a square post at their own canvas sizes, live text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes and every photograph embedded as image data, delivered with the self contained source HTML as the durable half. Paired with the price and availability formatting note, the field mapping verification record, the store naming rule, and the managers' persistent selects board.

verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count and extract the store identifier from each page, comparing the sequence against the reconciled roster.

verifiers_auto.text: Every price on every page matches that store's row in the cleaned sheet, and no price appears on a store's page that belongs to another store.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the price strings from each rendered page and diff them field by field against the merge dataset.

verifiers_auto.text: No page shows a dish line the sheet marks as not offered at that store, and no page shows an empty price, an orphaned leader rule or a naked dish name.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract each page's line inventory and compare against that store's availability flags, then scan for empty price fields and dangling rules.

verifiers_auto.text: Every placeholder the mapping claims to have written is genuinely present in the prepared template's stories.
verifiers_auto.how: Round trip the prepared template's document structure and search its stories for each expected field token.

verifiers_auto.text: Per store file names reproduce the roster exactly, including the two names the raw sheet carried with trailing whitespace, and each file's contents match the store its name claims.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the delivered filenames against the roster strings and read each file's store identifier and price set against its row.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered image exceeds its source pixel dimensions and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare each delivered image's dimensions against its source per the manifest and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero, and the cutouts carry genuine alpha rather than a cream rectangle.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG for a viewBox and a non spanning first path, and inspect each cutout's alpha channel for partial alpha at the subject boundary and full transparency at the corners.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned two slides each keeping its own declared canvas size, no image resolved to the importer's placeholder, and every text element carries a resolved licensed PostScript face.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide count and per slide dimensions from the export response, then parse the returned markup for placeholder image data and for the font family on every text node.

verifiers_auto.text: The four counter service rooms render from the counter card template with no plates section and no orphaned plate lines, and the combined estate PDF places every room in its roster slot with the counter rooms interleaved rather than clumped at the end.
verifiers_auto.how: Detect the template each page was built from by its structure, confirm the counter pages carry no plates story, and check the page sequence against the reconciled roster.

verifiers_auto.text: Every page's footer carries that room's own address and hours joined from the directory, no page merges with a blank footer, and no page shows another room's address.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the footer text from each rendered page and diff address and hours field by field against that room's directory row, listing any blank footer against the roster.

verifiers_auto.text: No address, hours or on now line oversets or truncates at trim on any page, and no counter room's on now line names a plate its kitchenless room cannot serve.
verifiers_auto.how: Read each page's footer and feature frames for clipped text and compare the counter rooms' feature values against the plates list.

verifiers_human.text: The insert reads as a fourteen to twenty six dollar independent room rather than as a chain or as a tasting menu.
verifiers_human.how: Judge type scale, density, photograph treatment and how loudly the prices are set, against the stated band and guest.

verifiers_human.text: A store that does not offer a line reads as a shorter menu rather than as a menu with something missing.
verifiers_human.how: Compare a counter service room's page against a flagship kitchen's page at trim.

verifiers_human.text: Cutout edges hold on cream at trim, on the dark pours as well as on the light plates.
verifiers_human.how: View each silhouette at full resolution on the cream ground rather than on its original counter.

verifiers_human.text: The two licensed frames sit inside the house set rather than beside it.
verifiers_human.how: Lay all eight graded frames in a row and try to identify which two were bought.

verifiers_human.text: The mark still reads as the house kettle and ring at the size it actually prints on the insert.
verifiers_human.how: View a rendered insert at trim rather than the artwork at full canvas.

verifiers_human.how: Open a sample of the per store files and read each against its row in the sheet.

verifiers_human.how: Open a sample of the per store files from both the kitchen and counter tiers and read each footer against the store directory.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a variable data run and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and that surface cannot hand back a print file.
What a store that does not offer a line actually prints, decided in the data because the merge has no conditional logic and cannot suppress a line.
How the store names are cleaned and which spelling is canonical, since the filenames the managers receive are built from them.
A mapping strategy chosen from what the conversion actually exposes rather than from what the printed price column looks like.
Selection wording on the pin: naming the pin takes the plating, naming the enamel's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the insert, judged at reproduction size on the printed page rather than at full canvas.
Which stock frame to license, judged for whether its light can be brought to a walnut counter rather than for how it looks in a catalogue.
Whether the featured items are silhouetted or framed, which is the single decision that sets the register for the whole estate.
Which per record delivery route to use, given that one preserves record identity and one does not.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against warm, cozy and elevated without falling into either the rustic chalkboard cliche or the cold neutral default.
What to tell the printer about the edge, given that the supplied press file carries no bleed and none can be introduced from it.

Which rooms merge from the plates template and which from the counter card, given the four counter service rooms have no kitchen and a plates page with every plate suppressed is a broken page rather than a shorter menu.

How the two per tier runs combine into one estate PDF in roster order when each merge orders only its own subset, and how the store directory is joined to the price sheet so every room's footer and rotating line land on the right room and stay within its service model.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a menu. IDENTITY: these are fourteen real rooms with fourteen different rent driven price sets and their own availability, printed under a mark that must be RECOVERED off an enamel pin rather than reinvented, because a regenerated kettle is a different group's logo, and under dish photographs that are these rooms' own plates. SPEC: the deliverable is a run whose page count must equal a reconciled store count in roster order, where every price traces to a row, where an unavailable line must vanish without leaving a hole, and where fourteen correctly named single page files must each contain their own store, where the four kitchenless rooms must come from a second template rather than a plates page struck empty, and where each room's own address, hours and rotating on now line are joined from a second sheet onto the right room and clipped by no frame, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: what the client is buying is that next season is a sheet update rather than fourteen retypings, so the artifact is a live merge template plus an editable counter card, not artwork. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this bought frame belong beside the house set, does this cutout edge hold on cream, does the file named for Burlington actually contain Burlington.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, with asset upload headless through initialize, PUT and finalize. One record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page count equal to row count and pages in CSV order, per row image binding through an at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified to bind different images to different records, per record separate files are verified in correct order via createSeparateFiles and via a recordRange loop, and true 300 DPI raster comes from document_render_layout rather than from the merge call. Checkpoint three rests on two documented findings together: multi record raster output URLs came back REVERSED while their labels claimed row order, and outputSpecs.resolution is silently ignored so a 300 request returned a 72 DPI page. The availability constraint rests on the verified absence of any conditional logic and on multiple records on one page being impossible. The bleed statement rests on the verified finding that a PDF derived template carries no bleed and none can be introduced. The two template split rests on convert_pdf_to_indd, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout each being verified to run per template, so two press files become two prepared templates and two runs, with the counter tier bound with no additionalImageFiles because its converted structure exposes no graphic frame; combining the two per tier runs into one roster ordered PDF is document assembly over verified per tier outputs, the directory join is data preparation over two CSVs into one merge source per tier, the joined non numeric footer and feature bind through the same text placeholder route already verified for the price and dish fields, and non numeric field overset is a property of a fixed converted frame meeting a variable length string, visible in the merged document's overset state and at the render rather than a new capability. STOCK: short generic queries only, orientation never passed because it always returns zero hits, renditionURL is a 240 px thumbnail only, and asset_license_and_download_stock returned a genuine 7360x4912 full resolution file, which is exactly why checkpoint one can only fire after download. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, remove_background and vectorize are verified across 27 live calls, including material and texture selection by prompt, the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the compound mark partial selection, the solid disc failure on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero. Alpha survives crops at outputFileType png, so the silhouettes are real. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as page one only. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. BOARDS: persistence verified with a hard cap of twelve placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no pdfPreset, no bleed claim, no upscaling, no OCR, no text to image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty.
